author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Manchester police have charged a 24-year-old woman with aggravated driving under the influence and endangering the welfare of a child after a Monday evening crash that seriously injured her 1-year-old daughter.

According to court documents reported by Manchester Ink Link, Brianne Gonzalez was driving a Toyota RAV4 south on Belmont Street when it went through a stop sign and collided with a Cadillac traveling west on Hanover Street. The RAV4 rolled onto its side, ejecting Gonzalez while the toddler remained trapped inside.

Both mother and child suffered brain bleeds. The child also sustained a fractured skull and was airlifted from Elliot Hospital to Boston Children’s Hospital. Two other occupants of the RAV4 and the Cadillac driver were also taken to hospitals. Gonzalez remained hospitalized when the charges were filed.

An arrest affidavit said a blood draw taken shortly after the crash showed a blood-alcohol concentration of .246. Bail was set on personal recognizance with restrictions on contact with the child unless supervised by a sober adult over 25. Manchester’s Collision Analysis Reconstruction Team continues to investigate the crash.
dek: Court documents say a Monday collision left a 1-year-old with a fractured skull and her mother and several others injured.
headline: Manchester woman charged with aggravated DUI after crash injures toddler
